originalTitle: After 7 months, Glasswing overwelms maintainers with underwhelming findings
content:
We're seven months into Anthropic's flagship Project Glasswing, and it's time for another update on the results. I've been tracking the project to see whether its claims are overhyped or grounded in reality.

As we all recall, Anthropic launched Project Glasswing on April 7th, claiming, "We have identified thousands of additional high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities that we are working on responsibly disclosing to open source maintainers." What surprised me was how little evidence the project offered, which made me wonder whether this was more of an overhyped marketing campaign.

That said, we shouldn't overlook that AI is an effective tool for finding vulnerabilities. But that story goes well beyond any single frontier model's capabilities.

If you're just catching up, this builds on my earlier posts:

Tracking Anthropic-Discovered Vulnerabilities

I started tracking Anthropic's discovered vulnerabilities on April 17th, shortly after launch, in an open source repo called code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 hover:[&>code]:border-primary hover:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> Anthropic Credited CVEs . The goal was to see whether Anthropic's claims lived up to the hype. This was before Anthropic launched its own code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 hover:[&>code]:border-primary hover:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> disclosure ledger , which is only updated in infrequent bulk batches.

My repo tracks every vulnerability attributable to Anthropic using CVE records, GHSAs, Linux kernel commits, and Anthropic's own ledger. I also manually audit advisories to catch CVEs that might otherwise get overlooked.

After seven months, I've tracked 442 CVEs attributable to Anthropic. That's an average of just 63 per month. Out of the 93,450 CVEs published this year, that's only about 0.5% of all CVEs.

For comparison, Anthropic's own public ledger lists just 217 fixed vulnerabilities, so I've tracked more than twice as many as Anthropic has disclosed itself.

The Danger Narrative Isn't Adding Up

You may recall that Glasswing launched with the message that we'd entered the Mythos era of vulnerability discovery. But are these vulnerabilities actually useful to attackers? To find out, I've been tracking Anthropic-discovered CVEs against VulnCheck KEV. So far, only 2 of the 442 have been exploited in the wild, just 0.45%. (CVE-2026-61500 and CVE-2026-26980)

Anthropic's Ledger Continues to Underwhelm

When Anthropic first launched its ledger in May, it reported 23,019 findings and a 90.8% true positive rate. As of its most recent update on November 2nd, there are 37,966 findings and just 217 fixes. That looks like a staggering failure to me, but let's take a closer look.

Of the 37,966 findings Anthropic reports, only 7,349 (19.4%) have been made public. Just 217 of those have been marked fixed. The more glaring number is that 4.4% (1,654) of the project's findings have already been marked as duplicates, 7.5x more duplicates than fixes. On top of that, 419 findings have been withdrawn. It seems odd that the ledger now claims a 94.2% true positive rate, up from 90.8% at launch, when more findings have been withdrawn or marked as duplicates than fixed, likely a feedback loop missing to the triage rates listed as “True Positives”.

The trend since my September update is even more telling:

In two months, Anthropic added nearly 12,000 findings and fixed just 15 more. Duplicates went from two to thousands, which is exactly what I warned about in September: the longer findings sit, the more likely someone else finds and fixes them first. I don't know how anyone can read these numbers as anything but damning.

You may also notice a correction in my visual. There appears to be a bug on Anthropic's ledger that inflates the number of findings marked as disclosed. Check for yourself using the "disclosed" filter.

Having humans triage every finding clearly didn't scale, and Anthropic has said as much. In its code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 hover:[&>code]:border-primary hover:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> OSS Scanner launch post on October 8th, Anthropic said it had found more than 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities but had manually reviewed only about 6,000, and that it remains "bottlenecked on our human capacity to validate these findings." It had also already sent nearly 5,000 unverified reports to maintainers who asked for everything in bulk.

So with the Glasswing open source initiative hitting a wall, launching a self-service code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 hover:[&>code]:border-primary hover:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> OSS Scanner that projects can opt into makes sense. Maintainers can now request a scan and triage the findings themselves. Anthropic is upfront that these reports are "fully model-generated, without human review or triage" and that "it is possible reports will be incorrect or invalid."

In other words, the triage bottleneck didn't go away. It moved to the maintainers. If the true positive rate is really as high as Anthropic claims, that shouldn't be a problem.

chineseTitle: 7 个月后，Glasswing 的发现让维护人员大吃一惊
chineseContent:
Anthropic 的旗舰项目 Glasswing 已经开展了七个月，现在是时候再次更新结果了。我一直在跟踪该项目，看看它的说法是否被夸大或基于现实。

我们都记得，Anthropic 于 4 月 7 日启动了 Glasswing 项目，声称“我们已经发现了数千个额外的高严重性和关键严重性漏洞，我们正在负责任地向开源维护人员披露这些漏洞。”令我惊讶的是，该项目提供的证据如此之少，这让我怀疑这是否更像是一场过度炒作的营销活动。

也就是说，我们不应该忽视人工智能是发现漏洞的有效工具。但这个故事远远超出了任何单一前沿模型的能力。

如果您刚刚赶上，这建立在我之前的帖子的基础上：

追踪人类发现的漏洞

我于 4 月 17 日开始跟踪 Anthropic 在发布后不久在一个名为 code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 hide:[&>code]:border-primary hide:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary 的开源存储库中发现的漏洞focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> Anthropic 认可的 CVE 。目标是看看 Anthropic 的声明是否符合宣传。这是在 Anthropic 推出自己的 code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 之前href:[&>code]:border-primary hide:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> 披露分类帐 ，仅在不频繁的批量批次中更新。

我的存储库使用 CVE 记录、GHSA、Linux 内核提交和 Anthropic 自己的分类帐来跟踪可归因于 Anthropic 的每个漏洞。我还手动审核建议以捕获可能会被忽视的 CVE。

7 个月后，我跟踪了 442 个由 Anthropic 造成的 CVE。平均每月只有 63 个。在今年发布的 93,450 个 CVE 中，这仅占所有 CVE 的 0.5% 左右。

相比之下，Anthropic 自己的公共账本仅列出了 217 个已修复的漏洞，因此我跟踪的漏洞数量是 Anthropic 自己披露的漏洞数量的两倍多。

危险的叙述并没有增加

您可能还记得 Glasswing 发布时传达的信息是我们已进入漏洞发现的神话时代。但这些漏洞真的对攻击者有用吗？为了找到答案，我一直在针对 VulnCheck KEV 跟踪 Anthropic 发现的 CVE。到目前为止，442 种中只有 2 种在野外被利用，仅占 0.45%。 （CVE-2026-61500 和 CVE-2026-26980）

Anthropic 的账本继续表现不佳

当 Anthropic 在 5 月份首次推出其账本时，报告了 23,019 项发现，真实阳性率为 90.8%。截至 11 月 2 日最新更新，已发现 37,966 项发现，仅修复 217 项。对我来说，这看起来是一个令人震惊的失败，但让我们仔细看看。

在人类报告的 37,966 项调查结果中，只有 7,349 项 (19.4%) 已公开。其中只有 217 个已标记为已修复。更引人注目的数字是，4.4% (1,654) 的项目发现已被标记为重复项，重复项比修复项多 7.5 倍。除此之外，419 项调查结果已被撤回。奇怪的是，账本现在声称的真阳性率为 94.2%，高于发布时的 90.8%，当时撤回或标记为重复的结果多于修复的结果，这可能是列为“真阳性”的分类率缺少反馈循环。

自我九月更新以来的趋势更加明显：

在两个月内，Anthropic 添加了近 12,000 个发现结果，仅修正了 15 个。重复项从两个增加到数千个，这正是我在 9 月份警告的：发现的时间越长，其他人就越有可能首先找到并修复它们。我不知道怎么会有人把这些数字解读为不该死的。

您可能还会注意到我的视觉效果有所修正。 Anthropic 的账本上似乎存在一个错误，导致标记为已披露的调查结果数量增加。使用“公开”过滤器自行检查。

让人类对每一个发现进行分类显然无法扩大规模，Anthropic 也说了同样的话。在其代码中]：outline-0 [&>代码]：border-dashed [&>代码]：outline-primary/25 focus-visible：[&>代码]：outline-3悬停：[&>代码]：border-primary悬停：[&>代码]：text-primary focus-visible：[&>代码]：border-primary focus-visible：[&>代码]：text-primary过渡颜色[&>code]:transition-colors"> OSS 扫描程序在 10 月 8 日发布后，Anthropic 表示已发现超过 29,000 个候选漏洞，但手动审查的仅约 6,000 个，而且“它仍然是“我们验证这些发现的人力能力的瓶颈”。它还已经向要求批量提供所有内容的维护人员发送了近 5,000 份未经验证的报告。

因此，随着 Glasswing 开源计划碰壁，推出了自助服务 code]:outline-0 [&>code]:border-dashed [&>code]:outline-primary/25 focus-visible:[&>code]:outline-3 hide:[&>code]:border-primary hide:[&>code]:text-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:border-primary focus-visible:[&>code]:text-primary transition-colors [&>code]:transition-colors"> 项目可以选择使用的 OSS 扫描仪是有意义的。维护人员现在可以请求扫描并自行对结果进行分类。 Anthropic 坦言这些报告“完全由模型生成，无需人工审查或分类”，并且“报告可能不正确或无效”。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于 AI 与科技趋势信号，适合用于观察工具选型、产品机会、开发者关注点和技术路线变化。
